baseline:
B
A standard transformer block is composed of a multi-head attention mechanism followed by a position-wise feed-forward neural network (an MLP).

B
An MLP is defined by having at least one hidden layer between the input and output layers. The non-linear activation functions within these layers are crucial, as they allow the network to learn complex, non-linear patterns in data.

B
The MLP (Multi-Layer Perceptron), or feed-forward network, in a transformer block takes the context-aware embeddings produced by the attention mechanism and applies a non-linear transformation. This step allows the model to further process the information and learn more complex representations for each token.

C
The weights of the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) are adjusted during training to map specific input patterns (keys) to desired output patterns (values), effectively encoding facts as learned associations.

C
The weights (W) and biases (b) are the parameters of the model that are adjusted during the training process. This tuning process encodes the learned patterns from the data directly into the numerical values of W and b, which is how the network "stores" information.
